desc:
Funnel maintenance keeps your pages, forms and follow-ups working after launch. Ecom Swift LLC starts with a care sprint in your own accounts: we test every step as a visitor, fix what is broken, refresh offers and wording, and confirm that your follow-up emails still send.

## What is funnel maintenance?

Funnel maintenance is the regular checking and updating of the path that turns visitors into leads. It covers pages, forms, booking links, alert emails, CRM entries and automated follow-ups. The aim is to find faults before a customer does.

A care sprint is the first round of that work. It is a focused block in which we test, repair and refresh, then give you a log of what changed.

## Why funnels quietly stop working

Funnels rarely fail with a loud crash. A form connection breaks after a plugin update. A booking link points to an old calendar. An offer expires but the page still advertises it. An alert email lands in spam, and enquiries pile up unseen.

Each of these problems can sit for weeks because everything looks fine from the owner's side. Meanwhile visitors hit dead ends and leave without a word. Regular testing is the only reliable way to catch them.

## How care improves your results

A working funnel loses fewer visitors to avoidable faults. Fixing a broken form or link recovers leads you were already paying to attract. Fresh wording and current offers keep the page believable, and a refreshed follow-up sequence keeps your replies timely and relevant.

Care also gives you a calmer way to run the business. With a log and a priority list, you know what changed and what to watch. Results still depend on your market and traffic, but a checked funnel cannot be blamed for losses that could have been prevented.

## What a good care sprint includes

- A full walk through the funnel on both a phone and a computer.
- A test submission of every form, booking and call button.
- A check that alert emails arrive and CRM entries are created.
- Repairs to broken links, forms and redirects.
- Updates to out-of-date offers, dates, prices and wording.
- A review of follow-up emails for tone, timing and accuracy.
- A speed and mobile check on the main pages.
- An optional look at recent lead data, where the package includes it.
- A written change log.
- A short list of what to watch and what to do next.

## What we do

We begin by agreeing which funnel or funnels to check and gaining access to the pages, forms and tools involved. We then act as a first-time visitor, using real test enquiries and noting everything that does not work or reads badly. After that, we fix the faults and make the content updates your package covers.

Higher packages include more funnels, more text and content updates, a refresh of follow-up emails, a speed check and a redesign of one page section. The largest package also reviews recent lead data and ends with a handover call and a plan for the next sprint. Monthly care after the sprint is offered separately, and we explain what it would include before you decide.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Test your own funnel every month as if you were a stranger.
- Update offers and dates as soon as they change.
- Keep a record of every change to forms and automations.
- Make sure someone receives the alert emails and reads them.
- Ask for a check after any website update or tool change.

**Avoid:**
- Assuming a form still works because it worked at launch.
- Leaving old offers on pages after they have ended.
- Changing several things at once with no record.
- Ignoring slow pages on mobile.
- Leaving problems unnoticed until a lead or customer tells you about them.

## Who this service is for

This service suits an owner whose funnel was built a while ago and has not been checked since. It also suits a business that changed its website, email tool or CRM and wants to confirm that nothing broke. A funnel built by someone else, with no clear handover notes, is another good fit.

## What we need from you

Send the links to your pages, forms and booking tools, plus a list of the offers and details that have changed. We never need passwords. Access is given to us as a collaborator, staff, team or developer user in the platforms involved, and we work only inside your own accounts.
